newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia's ComTrade, IBM sign dealership agreement.
newsitem.headline: Serbia's ComTrade, IBM sign dealership agreement.

text.p: Serbia's computer retailer ComTrade of Belgrade has signed a deal with IBM of London to market IBM personal computers, equipment and point of sales systems in Yugoslavia.
The agreement was signed on Thursday by ComTrade Group President Veselin Jevrosimovic and IBM manager for Yugoslavia Michael Strang.
The distributorship deal will provide Yugoslav customers with a better offer, higher quality and speedier delivery of the latest IBM products under favourable conditions, Jevrosimovic said.
"Through this cooperation deal, Comtrade's customers will also have access to powerful super-servers from the IBM RS-6000 series," ComTrade Special Projects Manager Ivan Ivkovic told Reuters.
Comtrade was founded in 1991 in Miami and later moved to Yugoslavia to become a prominent name on the local computer market, using a network of around 400 dealers throughout the country.
According to unofficial data, ComTrade, which employs 35 people, accounted for around 52 percent of computer sales on the Yugoslav market last year.
No other sales figures or details were available.

Local papers last November reported IBM had signed a deal with foreign trade firm Vobex of Novi Sad, a subsidiary of Vojvodjanska Banka, to market PCs and equipment primarily for the needs of banks and other financial organisations. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
